persistence_invariants.brief: A composite unique constraint on (sku, location) guarantees each SKU at each location is uniquely addressable; a duplicate insert is rejected at write time, never two stored rows (R3).
A CHECK constraint (quantity >= 0) prevents a stored negative stock level; a pick that would overcommit is rejected at write time (R2).
sku, location, quantity, and inventory_code are NOT NULL so a stock record cannot be persisted missing a required field (AC1 durable capture).
Each record/adjustment carries a NOT NULL, unmodifiable created_at timestamp and actor, preserving audit provenance across migrations (R1).
The Alembic migration is additive and reversible; existing inventory records survive every schema migration with no loss (R1).

nfrs.brief: Existing stock data survives every additive schema migration with no loss; each adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp and actor. Defended by the migration-reversibility fitness test and PI4/PI5 branch integration tests.

Stock never stored below zero and never overcommitted; a pick that would overcommit is rejected at write time. Enforced by the service layer plus the PI2 CHECK constraint, verified by a real-branch integration test.

Every (sku, location) pair is uniquely addressable; a collision is resolved at write time, never two stored duplicates and never an error page. Defended by the PI1 composite unique constraint and a branch integration test.

Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL), never a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch. Defended by the real-DB fitness function.

The UI is a React + TypeScript single-page app under client/ with client-side navigation and optimistic in-place row updates; the boundary layer returns JSON, not server-rendered HTML. Boundary declared renders_via react; client ships its own component tests, the API is covered by R4 branch integration tests.
Validation errors name the offending field (not a generic 'bad request'), owned at the API boundary. From nfrs.md Preferences.
A stock row missing optional detail (par level, batch, serial) renders cleanly showing an explicit 'not tracked', never a null crash or blank region. From nfrs.md Preferences.
